newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan car shares driven higher by weakening yen.
newsitem.headline: Japan car shares driven higher by weakening yen.

text.p: Shares in Japan's automobile sector rose on Monday morning, driven higher by the yen's weakening against the dollar, brokers said.
As of 0118 GMT, Toyota Motor Corp was 40 yen higher at 3,600 on turnover totalling 1.56 million shares, making it the third-most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.
Mazda Motor Corp was up 23 yen at 444 and Honda Motor Co Ltd rose 90 yen to 3,810.

"Foreign investors especially are actively buying car maker shares, helped by the weakening yen, but domestic investors are queuing up to sell shares in companies such as Toyota," a broker at a "Big Four" brokerage said.
"Some investors are apprehensive about the growth of the sector on a mid-term basis," the broker added.
